newsitem.title: USA: Kodak to split Asia Pacific region.
newsitem.headline: Kodak to split Asia Pacific region.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. said Monday it would divide its existing Asia Pacific region into two new regions to help it focus on Japan, the second largest photography market in the world.
Japan will be one region and Asia Pacific will be the other, the company said.

The company also said Robert Smith, vice president and general manager of its Asia Pacific region, would retire effective April 1, 1997, but would head the new Japan region until then, while Kodak searches for a replacement.

Edward Hoppe, vice president and general manager, marketing companies, for Kodak's European, African and Middle Eastern Region, was named vice president and general manager of the new Asia Pacific region, it said.
Kodak said Japan warranted greater focus since it was the second largest photography market in the world.
The Asia Pacific region, to be headquartered in Singapore, would consist of eastern Asia, excluding Japan and greater China, which constitutes a separate region, plus Australia and New Zealand.
Hoppe will be replaced by David Wilson, general manager of Kodak's Nordic cluster, Kodak said.
Kodak stock closed at $75.875, down 25 cents, Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.
